chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, he said: He narrated to me Abu Abdullah al-Razi, from al-Hasan ibn al-Husayn al-Lu'lu'i, from al-Husayn ibn Yusuf, from al-Hasan ibn Ziyad al-Attar

Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: Three [groups of people] are in the protection of God, the Exalted, until God finishes with the Reckoning: a man who has never committed adultery, a man who has never mixed his wealth with usury, and a man who has never strived in them [committing these two deeds].
ai.seo_question: Who are the three groups of people protected by God until the Reckoning according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq records this hadith to highlight the comprehensive nature of divine protection (*hirz*), extending beyond mere avoidance of the sin itself to include the prevention of its active pursuit. This triad of purity—chastity, financial integrity, and intent—serves as a spiritual shield against the terrors of the Day of Judgment, emphasizing that true righteousness involves both action and intention. The narration underscores the Shia emphasis on *tawqif* (divine specification) in defining the criteria for salvation, linking moral conduct directly to eschatological security.
